translationRepairs: Li Zhouyi then marched from Bin and Fang to relieve Qi and camped on the Sanyuan frontier; Huaiying drove him off and took Zhai prefecture on the way back.
Li Zhouyi then came with Fu-Fang troops to relieve Qi and camped on the Sanyuan frontier; Huaiying drove him off and took Zhai prefecture on the way back.
鄜坊 denotes the Fu-Fang military region and its troops; the existing Bin reading confuses 鄜 with 邠. The proposed wording accurately renders 以鄜坊兵.
Huaiying took Ning, Qing, and Yan, but on the march back through Shengping Zhijun struck from cover and broke him.
Huaiying took Ning, Qing, and Yan, but on the march back through Shengping, Zhijun struck from cover and broke him.
The comma correctly separates the place 升平 (Shengping) from the following subject 知俊 (Zhijun).

Rain stopped Xun at Leeping and forced him back. He raced to Linqing for Wei’s grain stores, but Zhou Dewei was already there; Xun fell back to Shen county, built a supply road to the river, and fed his men.

Rain stopped Xun at Leping and forced him back. He raced to Linqing for Wei’s grain stores, but Zhou Dewei was already there; Xun fell back to Shen County, built a supply road to the river, and fed his men.

樂平 should be Leping, but the proposal wrongly changes 莘縣 to Xin County. In this Five Dynasties campaign context 莘縣 is Shen County in present-day Shandong, so the existing Shen reading must be retained.
Suo Qing was profoundly filial; mourning his father he wasted away in grief, and neighbors praised him.
Sui Qing was profoundly filial; mourning his father he wasted away in grief, and neighbors praised him.
The surrounding biography repeatedly names this man 遂清 as Sui Qing; 'Suo Qing' is an inconsistent mistransliteration.
As prefect of Zibo he went to meet his mother; when she reached the suburbs he took the reins and walked beside her carriage for miles—the whole prefecture counted it an honor.
As prefect of Zibo, Sui Qing went to meet his mother; when she reached the suburbs he took the reins and walked beside her carriage for miles—the whole prefecture counted it an honor.
遂清 remains the explicit subject of the episode. Restoring Sui Qing removes ambiguity and keeps the established reading used immediately above.
At the Last Emperor’s accession Cunjie became co-equal of the Secretariat and was posted to Tianshang.
At the Last Emperor’s accession Cunjie became co-equal of the Secretariat and was posted to Tianping.
The source has 天平, the Tianping military command; Tianshang is a transcription error.
When Jin attacked Wei, Guiba followed Ge Congzhou to the relief; they fought at the Huan River, and Guiba captured Kkuser's son Luoluo and gave him to the Wei garrison.
When Jin attacked Wei, Guiba followed Ge Congzhou to the relief; they fought at the Huan River, and Guiba captured Keyong's son Luoluo and gave him to the Wei garrison.
克用 refers to Li Keyong, Luoluo's father. 'Kkuser' is corrupted text with no basis in the Chinese.
Wang Chongshi came from Changshe in Xuzhou.
Wang Chongshi came from Changshe in Xu Prefecture.
許州 is Xu Prefecture, centered on Changshe; Xuzhou would represent 徐州 and identifies a different place.
When Qin Zongquan seized Xuzhou, Chongshi slipped away to Liang, followed Taizu against Cai, stormed Yan and Yanzhou, and commanded the Uproot-Mountains Army.
When Qin Zongquan seized Xu Prefecture, Chongshi slipped away to Liang, followed Taizu against Cai, stormed Yan and Yun, and commanded the Uproot-Mountains Army.
The proposed wording correctly distinguishes 許州 as Xu Prefecture and 兗、鄆 as Yan and Yun.
When Taizu held Xuanyi, Huaiyu commanded the garrison at Yongcheng.
When Taizu held Xuanwu, Huaiyu commanded the garrison at Yongcheng.
The command named in the source is 宣武, Xuanwu; Xuanyi is a different name.
With Taizu east against Yan and Yanzhou he broke Xu and Su.
With Taizu east against Yan and Yun he broke Xu and Su.
兗、鄆 names Yan and Yun; expanding the second as Yanzhou duplicates Yan and mistranslates 鄆.
Born Cong, he received the name Huaiyu from Taizu.
His original name was Cong; Taizu bestowed the name Huaiyu.
本名琮 explicitly says his original name was Cong. The proposed sentence is clearer and avoids the misleading compressed phrase 'Born Cong.'
